summary.text: A 32-year-old Filipino female who had been hospitalized twice in 2 months for palpitations and had viral myocarditis 4 months earlier presented a third time with progressive palpitations and a 3-day generalized rash. Heart rate was 141 bpm and blood pressure 85/48 mmHg, with erythematous plaques, sinus tachycardia on ECG, mild normocytic anemia and moderate proteinuria.

She was first treated for possible anaphylaxis, then for possible sepsis with empirical piperacillin/tazobactam, but tachycardia persisted; the Discussion states she required medical ICU admission for tachycardia-induced hypotension. Echocardiography showed a normal ejection fraction without effusion and CT pulmonary angiogram ruled out embolism. Positive ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro and anti-Scl-70 led to a diagnosis of SLE.

Acute psychosis developed with a brain MRI and cerebrospinal fluid analysis free of abnormality. Pulse methylprednisolone and hydroxychloroquine were given, her heart rate fell from 150 to 95 bpm and the psychosis resolved. A kidney biopsy showed focal lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS Class III. She was discharged on mycophenolate, hydroxychloroquine and prednisolone 20 mg, and at 2-month follow-up her heart rate was normal at around 83 bpm.
